newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France details pilots pay plan.
newsitem.headline: Air France details pilots pay plan.

text.p: A new pilots' pay scale proposed by state-owned Air France will take flying experience into account, using the same system as British Airways Plc, the airline said on Tuesday.
Pilot unions, apart from the SPAC, went on strike on Tuesday to protest against a plan to introduce a two-tier pay system aimed at cutting the wage bill. The strike runs to Friday.

New hires with more than 3,000 hours of flying time will get an annual gross salary of 320,000 francs ($55,900) in the first two years of service, while less experienced pilots will be paid 240,000 francs in the first year, Air France said.
The 450 student pilots trained by the group and who will be hired between now and 1999 will be paid on the basis of experienced crews.
The last crews hired by Air France were paid annual gross salaries of 350,000 francs.
The new pay conditions are due to go into effect in June but only the SPAC union has signed an agreement with the company and withdrawn its members from the current strike.
The other five labour unions, including the powerful SNPL which represents 80 percent of Air France pilots, are contesting the agreement.

"In trying to undermine the strike by signing a secret agreement with the SPAC, a union which represents only a tenth of Air France pilots and none at Air Inter Europe, (chairman) Christian Blanc is once again running a risk of failure," the five unions said in a statement.
"The management has not yet told the other unions the contents of the agreement, which it has reached in the greatest secrecy," they said.
The present strike by Air France pilots had been postponed from March 23, after Blanc had threatened to resign if the stoppage went ahead.
Air France maintained half of its short- and medium-haul flights and all its international routes on Tuesday.
The company has warned that each strike day costs 100 million francs and could wipe out the projected 500 million franc net profit expected for the 1997/98 year. ($ = 5.721 French Francs)
